title: Best Arctrieval Alternatives for Legal Medical Record Retrieval (2026)
summary: Comparing Arctrieval alternatives? See how Codes Health, YoCierge, RRS, ChartRequest, and others compare on retrieval timelines, AI analysis, integrations, and pricing.
body_markdown:
When plaintiff law firms look at Arctrieval alternatives, the choice usually comes down to this: do you want software that helps your team manage retrieval workflows, or a service that works toward complete records and adds AI-powered litigation insights? Arctrieval offers a software-based approach for firms managing retrieval in-house, but many legal teams want something that goes beyond workflow management, with AI analysis, human verification, and proactive gap detection. This guide walks through the top Arctrieval alternatives, with a close look at how[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) supports pre-litigation work with AI-powered medical record retrieval aimed at complete records in a couple of weeks.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health stands out as a leading Arctrieval alternative, pairing retrieval with AI-powered insights that flag potential breach-of-care indicators, pre-existing conditions, and documented future medical expenses for attorney review


-


Retrieval timelines are measured differently: Codes Health advertises retrieval in a couple of weeks, while Arctrieval reports that firms following its methodology can receive 90% of records within 30 days, so compare what each metric actually measures


-


Codes Health publishes claims of[80% less manual review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) and 50% more case capacity; these are company-reported results, and individual results may vary


-


Same-day claims need context. Some vendors use "same-day" for request submission and others for access to certain records. Codes Health's position is that same-day services often don't get complete records and need client involvement, which leads to churn


-


Missing-record detection matters: Codes Health advertises it, so compare each provider's completeness checks, outstanding-request tracking, and process for obtaining missing documents


-


General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and any AI-generated analysis needs verification against source records


## **Why Law Firms Seek Arctrieval Alternatives**


Arctrieval provides software that helps law firms manage medical-record request workflows internally. The software model gives firms control over the process while automating follow-up tasks and providing status dashboards.


**Why Firms Explore Alternatives:**


Even with Arctrieval's workflow benefits, plaintiff firms look at alternatives for several reasons:


-


Arctrieval's reviewed public materials focus on request management and follow-up rather than AI-generated medical analysis or chronologies


-


Firm staff operate the platform and handle exceptions in-house


-


Vendor-reported timelines measure different things, so firms want clarity on how long a complete case file actually takes


-


Some firms want potential breach-of-care indicators and other litigation insights surfaced for attorney review


-


Firms should confirm whether Arctrieval provides clinical gap detection beyond tracking outstanding requests and automating follow-up


## **Arctrieval**


Arctrieval is the baseline for this comparison. Its software helps law firms manage medical record retrieval internally, automating workflow tasks while keeping control within your firm.


**Platform Features:**


-


Unlimited retrieval request volume within subscription


-


Real-time status dashboard


-


Automated follow-up workflows


-


Individual Right of Access utilization


-


Arctrieval reports that firms following its methodology can receive 90% of records within 30 days; remaining requests may take longer


-


Arctrieval says its software can eliminate up to 80% of the time staff spend chasing incomplete or missing records


**Market Position:** Arctrieval's software model suits firms that want in-house staff running the retrieval process. In one published case study, KRA Legal, a California firm with three attorneys and 16 staff, cut request prep from 30 minutes to about 10 minutes per client and estimates roughly 50 hours of administrative work saved each month. When comparing vendors, note that the percentage returned within a deadline is a different measure from average retrieval time or time to complete an entire case file.


**Pricing:** Subscriptions are $155/month for one user, $279/month for five users, and $499/month for ten users. Listed one-time customer-success, training, and support fees are $339, $539, and $739 respectively. Fax usage above each plan's allowance costs $0.06 per page, and provider charges are paid separately by the firm.


**Best For:** High-volume firms that prefer in-house control over the retrieval process and have staff available to manage the platform.


The eight alternatives below are listed to help you compare service models. Codes Health is our featured pick.


## **1. Codes Health**


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) is built for plaintiff law firms that want more than a retrieval workflow. Unlike software-only solutions that require your team to manage the process, Codes Health combines AI-powered automation with human verification by medical and legal specialists, delivering records with case insights that support attorney and expert review.


**Why Codes Health Stands Apart:**


-


Retrieval in a couple of weeks through multiple outreach channels, including claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone; actual timing and completeness depend on the providers, authorizations, and records requested


-


AI-powered insights extraction that flags potential breach-of-care indicators, pre-existing conditions, documented future medical expenses, and treatment gaps for attorney review


-


Human verification that supports attorney and expert review of AI-generated findings


-


Missing Record Review that cross-references patient history to identify gaps before closing a request


-


Flat-fee pricing; confirm included services and any additional charges before ordering


**Key Capabilities:**


-


Automated case chronologies that organize records and group patient encounters and bills by visit


-


Pre-submission validation that catches authorization errors, missing dates, incorrect provider information, and absent signatures before rejection


-


Persistent provider follow-up across calls, faxes, emails, and portals until records arrive


-


Filevine integration to submit requests, track status, and receive records directly within Filevine case files


-


Custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume firms


**Catching Authorization Errors Early:**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can delay disclosure and force a resubmission. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


**A Platform That Keeps Evolving:**


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.


**Results Plaintiff Firms Report:**


Codes Health publishes[company-reported figures](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) of 80% less manual review and 50% more case capacity. These results aren't established as typical across AI-powered retrieval services, and individual results may vary.


**What Clients Say:**


Charles Brown, Managing Partner at Daly & Black, P.C., praises Codes Health's use of technology and its follow-through.


"I've been waiting for one partner to solve this pre-litigation side of the business." Kelman Harrel, Partner, Louis Law Firm


**Best For:**


Plaintiff firms handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, and wrongful death cases who want records paired with AI-powered analysis rather than documents that still need manual review.


## **2. YoCierge**


YoCierge positions itself as a concierge-style record retrieval service with extensive case management system integrations.


**Platform Features:**


-


12 case management integrations including Filevine, Litify, SmartAdvocate, MyCase, CASEpeer, Neos, and Smokeball


-


Same-day dispatch for orders received before its stated 4 p.m. cutoff


-


ReChron for chronological organization, plus AI-generated document summaries highlighting injury and pain information and medical-expense tables


-


Vendor-reported ISO 27001 and ISO 22301 certification and SOC 2 Type 2 credentials


**Market Position:** YoCierge's same-day dispatch refers to internal order submission, not record delivery from providers, and actual turnaround depends on provider response times. Processing speed alone does not establish completeness. Ask how outstanding records are identified and pursued, and what participation is required from the firm or client. Confirm any additional analysis requirements directly with the company.


**Pricing:** Volume-based flat service fee with no per-page service fees; custodial charges are handled separately.


**Best For:** Firms that prioritize the number of case management integrations and want a concierge-style service handling follow-up tasks.


## **3. Record Retrieval Solutions (RRS)**


Record Retrieval Solutions was founded in 2014 and offers retrieval services with published pricing. Its founder and leadership team bring decades of industry experience.


**Platform Features:**


-


$45 service fee per request (published rate)


-


Vendor-reported 15-day average turnaround


-


HIPAA compliance review included


-


Deficiency tracking for incomplete records


**Market Position:** RRS offers a straightforward per-request model with verification and follow-up on incomplete records. Confirm subscription requirements, minimum commitments, and cancellation terms directly with RRS.


**Pricing:** The $45 service fee is a base cost. Provider copying fees, custodian fees, and other charges are billed separately and add to the total cost per retrieval.


**Best For:** Budget-conscious firms seeking transparent base pricing who can manage provider fee variability.


## **4. ChartRequest**


ChartRequest offers managed medical-record retrieval through CaseBinder, with retrieval specialists handling provider follow-up.


**Platform Features:**


-


Retrieval specialists who handle provider follow-up


-


Advertised average retrieval turnaround of 7 to 14 days, with timing varying by provider


-


Guided submission process to reduce errors


-


Verification included before delivery


**Market Position:** ChartRequest suits firms that want a managed service handling provider communication. Confirm compatibility with your case-management system and the available integration workflow directly with ChartRequest.


**Pricing:** ChartRequest advertises a CaseBinder trial at $35 per request for 90 days, followed by custom pricing. Confirm eligibility and how provider charges are handled.


**Best For:** Firms wanting a hands-off managed service where retrieval specialists handle provider communication.


## **5. American Retrieval**


American Retrieval, part of U.S. Legal Support since January 2025, offers retrieval services through an extensive provider network.


**Platform Features:**


-


Access to an extensive provider network


-


RecordsHub portal for requesting, tracking, and accessing records


-


Part of the larger U.S. Legal Support organization


-


Founded in 1993


**Market Position:** Being part of a larger organization may provide stability and resources. Confirm any required claims-system integrations directly with American Retrieval.


**Pricing:** Contact American Retrieval for current pricing.


**Best For:** Firms seeking a retrieval service backed by a large legal support organization with extensive provider relationships.


## **6. Compex Legal Services**


Compex Legal Services has provided record retrieval since 1972 and advertises more than 5,000 law firm customers nationwide.


**Platform Features:**


-


More than 50 years in the industry


-


Nationwide coverage


-


Managed retrieval supported by technology and AI-assisted workflows


-


Established relationships with providers


**Market Position:** Compex combines managed retrieval with technology-enabled workflows, including AI-assisted custodian communications and its Asabell medical-record summarization offering, backed by long operating experience and scale.


**Pricing:** Contact Compex for current pricing.


**Best For:** Firms preferring an established retrieval vendor with decades of experience.


## **7. Tavrn**


Tavrn focuses on integrating retrieval with demand letter generation, positioning itself as a records-to-demand solution.


**Platform Features:**


-


Integrated retrieval, chronology, and demand generation


-


Vendor-reported chronology turnaround under 24 hours (for analysis, not record retrieval)


-


Specialist review available


**Market Position:** Tavrn's rapid turnaround applies to chronology and demand generation once records are obtained, not to the retrieval process itself, which still depends on provider response times.


**Pricing:** Tavrn's current official materials describe retrieval pricing of $40 per request, excluding provider fees. Confirm current pricing and separate charges for analysis services directly with Tavrn.


**Best For:** Firms wanting an integrated workflow from records through demand letter generation who process high volumes of similar case types.


## **8. EvenUp**


EvenUp specializes in AI-generated demand packages and advertises more than 2,000 personal injury firm customers.


**Platform Features:**


-


Verdict database integration for comparable case references


-


Optional expert review


-


Demand package generation


-


PLAAS service that includes medical-record and bill retrieval, document organization, and missing-item tracking


**Market Position:** EvenUp offers demand-generation tools and a broader PLAAS service that includes medical-record and bill retrieval. Firms should distinguish standalone drafting products from the managed PLAAS offering when comparing scope and pricing.


**Pricing:** Contact EvenUp for current pricing on its demand tools and PLAAS service.


**Best For:** Firms seeking demand packages with verdict database references, either alongside an existing retrieval workflow or through EvenUp's managed pre-litigation service.


## **Making the Right Choice for Your Firm**


The right alternative depends on your firm's needs, case volume, and priorities.


### **Consider Your Primary Pain Points**


**If your main challenge is retrieval speed:**


Codes Health advertises retrieval in a couple of weeks through multi-channel outreach and persistent follow-up. Some vendors use "same-day" to describe request submission, while others advertise same-day access to certain records, so confirm exactly what each claim measures. Codes Health's position is that services offering same-day retrieval often don't get the complete records, and filling the gaps requires client involvement that leads to churn. Codes Health gets complete records in weeks, not months.


**If you need AI-powered analysis:**


Several providers now offer some form of AI-assisted analysis.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) flags potential breach-of-care indicators, pre-existing conditions, and documented future expenses, with human verification. General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review, while Codes Health's AI platform is built to analyze medical records with high precision for legal use cases. Whatever tool you use, evaluate accuracy, omissions, source traceability, and human-review procedures before relying on outputs in legal work.


**If you want in-house control:**


Arctrieval's software model keeps the process within your firm, with staff operating the platform and handling exceptions.


**If CMS integration is paramount:**


YoCierge advertises 12 integrations, while Codes Health provides a Filevine integration plus custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume firms.


### **Evaluate Total Cost of Ownership**


Consider these cost factors beyond base pricing:


-


Provider fees: confirm whether the quoted fee includes provider and custodian charges or whether these are billed separately


-


Staff time: AI-powered platforms can reduce paralegal workload


-


Missing records: incomplete retrieval leads to additional requests, delays, and potential case issues


-


Analysis costs: manual chronology creation versus automated AI analysis


### **Assess Long-Term Value**


The retrieval decision shapes how well a case is prepared. Catching missing records and treatment gaps early gives your team more time to address them before demands and negotiations. Consider how retrieval quality and AI insights affect your settlement preparation and trial readiness.


For most plaintiff firms, the deciding question is whether the records that come back are complete, organized, and ready to build a case on. That's where Codes Health stands apart: AI validation before submission, persistent multi-channel follow-up, completeness checks before delivery, human-verified insights, flat-fee pricing, and a native Filevine workflow, all aimed at complete records in weeks, not months.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes Codes Health different from Arctrieval?**


Arctrieval provides software for managing retrieval in-house, with public materials focused on request management and follow-up. Codes Health is a retrieval and analysis service that delivers records with AI-powered insights, including potential breach-of-care flags, pre-existing condition flagging, and future medical expense extraction, supported by human verification. Arctrieval reports that firms following its methodology can receive 90% of records within 30 days, while Codes Health advertises retrieval in a couple of weeks with proactive missing record detection. Because these metrics measure different things, compare them carefully.


### **Can same-day retrieval services deliver complete medical records?**


Some vendors use "same-day" to describe request submission, while others advertise same-day access to certain records, so confirm exactly what each claim measures. Processing speed alone does not establish completeness. Codes Health's position is that same-day services often don't get the complete records and need client involvement, which leads to churn.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) prioritizes completeness, using AI cross-referencing to identify missing records before closing a request.


### **Why can't I use ChatGPT or general AI to analyze medical records?**


General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review. Codes Health's AI platform is built to analyze medical records with high precision for legal use cases, with human verification by medical and legal professionals supporting attorney and qualified expert review. With any tool, AI-generated analysis requires verification against source records.


### **What integrations does Codes Health offer?**


Codes Health has a strategic partnership with Filevine, allowing firms to submit requests, track status, communicate with the team, and receive completed records directly within Filevine case files. For high-volume firms using other systems, Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software.


### **How does flat fee pricing compare to per-request pricing?**


Codes Health offers flat-fee pricing. Confirm the included services, provider charges, and any exclusions in the written quote. Per-request pricing, like RRS's $45 base fee, excludes provider copying fees and analysis, so total costs depend on the providers and services involved.


### **What practice areas does Codes Health support?**


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) serves plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death cases. The platform's AI analysis is tailored to legal case contexts, identifying facts relevant to damages, liability, and case strategy for each practice area.
